note_on_method: Two kinds of claim appear below and they are kept apart deliberately. Claims about the world - how many courts a park has, whether a court is dedicated or dual-striped, what the tennis centre charges - come from the City of Long Beach and are cited. Claims about our own coverage are facts about this dataset rather than about Los Angeles County, and are worded so a reader cannot mistake one for the other. This is the second county in California this directory has published in, and one city of it is on this page.

slots.coverage: One city in Los Angeles County is published here: Long Beach, with eight venues and forty-eight courts verified against the City's own pages, twenty-three of them dedicated to pickleball on the City's per-venue wording. Long Beach is the third California city on this site and the first in this county. The County holds the City of Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance, Santa Monica and many other municipalities, as well as parks run by the County itself, and not one of those has been read against a named source, so none appears anywhere on this site. Anaheim, which Long Beach's own page names as a neighbour, is in Orange County and is not read either. This page therefore describes one city's parks department and nothing more. Within Long Beach three City sites are named and not published. Somerset Park has a stated count, "Dual striping 8 pickleball on 2 tennis courts", at an address, "1500 E. Carson", that the Census geocoder places in the neighbouring city of Carson rather than in Long Beach. The Billie Jean King Tennis Center is credited with four shared-use courts on the City's pickleball page and "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted" on its own. Whaley Park's line has no number. Every published address was matched at house-number level, six by the Census address file and two by OpenStreetMap, and placed in Los Angeles County.
slots.distribution: What is verified in this county sits inside one city, and inside that city it splits on a fact the operator states on every line: whether a court is dedicated to pickleball or shared with something else. Twenty-three of the forty-eight are dedicated - eight at DeForest Park, four each at Silverado, Veterans and Marina Vista, two at Junipero Beach and one at Bayshore. The other twenty-five are eight lines on one tennis court at Veterans, four dual-striped courts "for either tennis or pickleball" at Marina Vista, two dual-striped at Bayshore, three "on a shared sports court" at El Dorado Park West and eight "shared-use" courts at the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center. Veterans Park is the largest venue by count at twelve; DeForest is the largest dedicated set at eight. Everything else a county page could sort by is thin. Lighting is stated at one venue, the tennis centre, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted"; the other seven carry no lighting answer either way. Price is stated at the same one venue, $5 per person for drop-in play and $10 per court per hour to reserve, and nowhere else; no venue in the county is called free, because the City does not write the word. Hours are stated at two: "Dawn to Dusk" at DeForest and 7 a.m. to 9:30 p.m. on weekdays at the tennis centre. Indoor or outdoor is stated nowhere, so this county has no indoor or outdoor breakdown at all. A player with a job has one stated evening of pickleball in Los Angeles County on these pages, and it is a Friday at a tennis centre.
slots.gaps: The honest position is that this is a Long Beach page under a county heading, and nothing here estimates the rest of the county. The City of Los Angeles has not been read, and Long Beach's own page says something about it - "LA City Parks has four dedicated, lighted pickleball courts and 34 shared-use courts", with eight more dedicated, lighted courts described as under development - which is quoted here as what Long Beach writes about its neighbour and is not used as a source for Los Angeles, because a city's courts publish from that city's own pages. Pasadena, Torrance and Santa Monica have not been read; nor have the County's own parks; nor have Cerritos and Lakewood, which the Long Beach page also names. The threshold is unchanged: three venues with a named source and a date. Inside Long Beach the gaps are of three kinds. One is a boundary: Somerset Park is a City of Long Beach park at an address the Census places in Carson, and it will publish the day the address resolves inside Long Beach, not before. One is contradiction: the Billie Jean King Tennis Center's four courts on one City page and eight on another, and the City's own total of "24 dedicated pickleball courts" against a list that adds to twenty-three. One is silence: no surface, no nets, no indoor-or-outdoor word, no price at any park, and lighting at one venue in eight. Nothing outside a municipal parks department appears on this page. Clubs, schools and commercial venues may hold courts across the county, and none of them publishes a source these pages have read.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there in Los Angeles County?
faqs.a: We do not know, and no honest page can tell you. What we have checked is 48 courts across eight venues, all in Long Beach, each with a source and a date you can see. The City of Long Beach itself names three more sites we cannot publish, and every other municipality in the county is unread.

faqs.q: Why is only Long Beach listed?
faqs.a: Because it is the only municipality in the county whose courts we have confirmed against a named source. A city appears here once three or more of its venues carry a source_url and a date_checked. Los Angeles, Pasadena, Torrance, Santa Monica and the County's own parks have not been read. Anaheim, which Long Beach's page names, is in Orange County.

One: the El Dorado Park Tennis & Pickleball Center, "8 Pickleball Courts, Fully Lighted", open until 9:30 p.m. on weekdays. The other seven Long Beach venues carry no lighting answer either way, and they are recorded as unverified rather than as unlit.

faqs.q: Are any of the courts free?
faqs.a: The City does not say so, and we do not assume it. Its park courts are first come, first served, which is a play format; the one stated price is at the tennis centre, $5 per person for drop-in play and $10 per court per hour to reserve. There is no free page for Los Angeles County.

faqs.q: What does "dedicated" mean here, and why do the totals differ?
faqs.a: Dedicated is the City's word for a court that is pickleball and nothing else, and Long Beach writes it or "dual-striped" on every line. Its per-venue dedicated figures add to 23; its own sentence says "Currently there are 24 dedicated pickleball courts in Long Beach." The list is published, not the total.

faqs.q: Why is Somerset Park not listed?
faqs.a: The City writes its address as "1500 E. Carson", and the Census geocoder places that in the neighbouring city of Carson, postcode 90745. The count is stated - eight dual-striped courts on two tennis courts - and the park is the City's; it fails on where the resolver puts it, and is re-read on every build.

faqs.q: How often is this checked again?
faqs.a: These pages were read on 7 September 2026, and every quoted sentence is snapshotted into the repository that builds this site and re-asserted on every build. If the City changes a count, reconciles the Billie Jean King numbers, or Somerset's address resolves inside Long Beach, the build fails and someone reads the page again.
